q: Most of the fluids are not ideal ones and offer some ____ to motion.
e: Most of the fluids are not ideal ones and offer some resistance to motion. resistance is the word that belongs in that blank.

q: The resistance to fluid motion (or) internal resistance of fluid is called ____.
e: The resistance to fluid motion (or) internal resistance of fluid is called viscosity. Viscosity is shear stress divided by velocity gradient, η = (F/A)/(dv/dy).

q: Viscosity arises when there is ____ motion between layers of the fluid.
e: Viscosity arises when there is relative motion between layers of the fluid. Viscosity is shear stress divided by velocity gradient, η = (F/A)/(dv/dy).

q: More precisely, it measures resistance to flow arising due to the internal friction between the fluid layers as they ____ past one another when fluid flows.
e: More precisely, it measures resistance to flow arising due to the internal friction between the fluid layers as they slip past one another when fluid flows. slip is the word that belongs in that blank.

q: Viscosity can also be thought of as a measure of a fluid's ____ (stickiness) or its resistance to objects passing through it.
e: Viscosity can also be thought of as a measure of a fluid's thickness (stickiness) or its resistance to objects passing through it. Viscosity is shear stress divided by velocity gradient, η = (F/A)/(dv/dy).

q: A fluid with large viscosity resists motion because its strong ____ forces give it a lot of internal friction.
e: A fluid with large viscosity resists motion because its strong intermolecular forces give it a lot of internal friction. Viscosity is shear stress divided by velocity gradient, η = (F/A)/(dv/dy).

q: A fluid with low viscosity flows easily because its molecular make up results in very little ____ when it is in motion.
e: A fluid with low viscosity flows easily because its molecular make up results in very little friction when it is in motion. Viscosity is shear stress divided by velocity gradient, η = (F/A)/(dv/dy).

q: The viscosity of liquids ____ rapidly with an increase in temperature, and the viscosity of gases increases with an increase in temperature.
e: The viscosity of liquids decreases rapidly with an increase in temperature, and the viscosity of gases increases with an increase in temperature. Viscosity is shear stress divided by velocity gradient, η = (F/A)/(dv/dy).

q: Thus, upon heating, liquids flow more easily, whereas gases flow more ____.
e: Thus, upon heating, liquids flow more easily, whereas gases flow more slowly. Heating raises gas viscosity, so gases flow more slowly.

q: Also, viscosity does not change as the amount of matter changes, therefore it is an ____ property.
e: Also, viscosity does not change as the amount of matter changes, therefore it is an intensive property. Viscosity is shear stress divided by velocity gradient, η = (F/A)/(dv/dy).

q: The SI unit of viscosity is ____ second (Pa s) which is equivalent to newton second per metre squared ($N s m^{-2}$).
e: The SI unit of viscosity is pascal second (Pa s) which is equivalent to newton second per metre squared (N s m⁻²). Viscosity is shear stress divided by velocity gradient, η = (F/A)/(dv/dy).

q: One way is to measure fluid's resistance to flow when an external force is applied. This is known as ____ viscosity.
e: One way is to measure fluid's resistance to flow when an external force is applied. This is known as dynamic viscosity. Viscosity is shear stress divided by velocity gradient, η = (F/A)/(dv/dy).

q: And the other way is to measure the resistive flow of a fluid under the weight of gravity. It is known as ____ viscosity.
e: And the other way is to measure the resistive flow of a fluid under the weight of gravity. It is known as kinematic viscosity. Viscosity is shear stress divided by velocity gradient, η = (F/A)/(dv/dy).

q: Newton's law of viscosity states that the shear stress between the two adjacent layers of fluid is directly proportional to the ____ value of the velocity gradient between the same two adjacent fluid layers.
e: The blank is negative. Viscosity is shear stress divided by velocity gradient, η = (F/A)/(dv/dy). That word is the one that completes the idea about Newton law viscosity states shear stress.

q: Shear stress is the shearing force per unit ____.
e: Shear stress is the shearing force per unit area. area is the word that belongs in that blank.

q: Viscosity is defined as the ratio of shearing stress to the ____ gradient.
e: Viscosity is defined as the ratio of shearing stress to the velocity gradient. Viscosity is shear stress divided by velocity gradient, η = (F/A)/(dv/dy).

q: Stokes' law expresses the ____ force resisting the fall of small spherical objects through a fluid medium under the influence of gravity.
e: Stokes' law expresses the drag force resisting the fall of small spherical objects through a fluid medium under the influence of gravity. Stokes' law gives the viscous drag on a small sphere as F = 6πηrv.

q: At a constant velocity of fall (terminal velocity), the upward and downward forces are in ____.
e: At a constant velocity of fall (terminal velocity), the upward and downward forces are in balance. balance is the word that belongs in that blank.
